observation.visible_scene: A single person with long dark braided hair, wearing a neon-yellow sleeveless top, pleated skirt, and yellow leg-warmers/socks, stands in a bright white dance studio facing a large wall mirror on the right. The camera is positioned behind her, so her back is to the viewer while the mirror shows her front reflection. She performs a sequence of upper-body arm movements against an otherwise static background (white walls, ceiling track lights, curtain, mirror frame).
visible_changes: At the start (frames 1-10) both arms are extended upward and outward in a wide diagonal V, held with only small positional shifts; the mirror reflection reproduces the same pose.
From about frame 11 to 20 the arms rotate inward toward a more vertical overhead position, hands rising near the top of the frame, while the torso stays oriented toward the mirror.
From about frame 21 to 30 the elbows bend and the hands drop from overhead down to head/shoulder level and then briefly in front of the chest, transitioning into a flexed-arm pose.
From about frame 31 to 41 the arms settle into a bent-at-the-sides position with hands/fists raised near shoulder height, with small up-and-down pumping movements continuing to the end of the clip.
Throughout, the feet make small weight shifts and steps (e.g., a heel lift visible in early frames, legs spread apart later), but the body does not turn away from the mirror.
The mirror image moves in lockstep with the real person, confirming it is a reflection of the same dancer rather than a second person.
The camera and background remain fixed; apparent motion is from the dancer's limbs and feet, not from camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: The purpose or name of the movement sequence (e.g., a specific dance or exercise routine) is not established by the clip.
Whether the arm motion had begun before frame 1 or continues after frame 41 is unknown; both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries.
Audio, music, or any external cue driving the rhythm is not visible.
The dancer's facial expression in the reflection is partially visible but its meaning/intent is not determinable.
uncertain_details: Exact hand shapes (open palms vs. fists) vary between frames and are hard to resolve at this resolution.

Minor differences in arm angles between consecutive frames could be small sway or deliberate movement; the overall trend (wide raised -> vertical -> bent flexed) is clear but individual micro-motions are uncertain.
Whether the foot shifts constitute steps in place or weight transfers is not fully distinguishable.
